daily.summary: Equinor is still restoring IT systems after a cyberattack that left oil and gas production untouched, and has not named an attacker. The FBI warned about an AI framework used to automate intrusions, and Google described a Russian FSB-linked group impersonating one US victim's staff to breach another. CISA flagged active exploitation of Perforce Puppet, the REDCap research platform used by hospitals and three other products, while F5 fixed five critical NGINX flaws. US intelligence, DHS and FBI officials told Congress that last week's run of outages, including an FAA ground stop, shows no sign of a cyberattack.

weekly.summary: The week's reporting centres on attackers using AI to speed up intrusions: the FBI, Google and Unit 42 all describe autonomous attack frameworks in real operations. State-linked activity includes North Korean financial theft, Russian espionage against Romanian government email and two US organizations, and a reported China-linked intrusion at a European telecom provider. Equinor's IT outage is the week's most notable incident at an allied energy operator, with production reported unaffected. A steady run of exploited or critical flaws in Java, NGINX, Puppet, REDCap, Cisco BroadWorks and refrigeration controllers keeps patching pressure high, while officials say recent US outages were not attacks.
